question: You are building a content-ingestion pipeline that uses Azure Language in Foundry Tools to detect the language of user-submitted forum posts. One post contains the text "I know a cool AI developer. He has a certain je ne sais quoi!". What does the language detection API return for this document?

options.text: The language with the largest representation in the content (English), but with a lower confidence score
An error, because mixed-language documents are rejected by the service
Two language entries (en and fr), each with its own confidence score
The language name and ISO code as (unknown) with a confidence score of 0

explanation: Mixed-language content within a single document returns the language with the largest representation in the content, but with a lower positive rating that reflects the marginal strength of the assessment. The service returns a single primary language per document, not one entry per language. The (unknown) result with score 0 is returned only when the analyzer cannot parse the content at all (for example because of character-encoding issues).

Transcription runs in real time in a mobile app. What should you do to improve accuracy, and what is required before the app can use the result?

options.text: Switch to a gpt-4o-transcribe deployment and add the product codes to the SSML phoneme element
Train a custom speech model with related text (and optionally audio with reference transcripts), then deploy it to a custom endpoint, which is required for real-time recognition
Train a custom speech model and use it directly from the base-model endpoint; custom endpoints are only needed for batch transcription
Enable the Speech MCP server profanity filter set to raw so domain terms are not masked

explanation: A custom speech model augments the Universal Language base model to improve recognition of domain-specific vocabulary by training with text data (and audio with reference transcriptions for specific acoustic conditions). After testing, you deploy the model to a custom endpoint; except for batch transcription, you must deploy a custom endpoint to use a custom speech model; the claim that custom endpoints are only needed for batch transcription has it backwards. Word error rate (WER) on test data tells you whether more training is needed.

question: You are defining a JSON Schema for structured outputs with an Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models deployment (response_format type json_schema with strict set to true). Which three rules must the schema follow? (Choose three.)

options.text: The schema may have up to 100 object properties in total and up to five levels of nesting
String properties should use minLength and maxLength to constrain output size
The root object may be an anyOf of several alternative objects
All properties must be listed in the required array; optional values are emulated with a union type that includes null
Every object must set additionalProperties to false

explanation: Structured outputs support a subset of JSON Schema: every object must set additionalProperties: false, all fields must be required (an optional field is emulated with a type such as ["string", "null"]), and a schema can have up to 100 object properties with up to five levels of nesting. minLength, maxLength, pattern and format are explicitly unsupported string keywords, and root objects cannot be the anyOf type.

In the tools array as a function with strict set to true
In the text.format property, with type json_schema, name, schema and strict as siblings
In the response_format property, exactly as with Chat Completions

explanation: Both APIs support structured outputs, but the schema location differs: Chat Completions uses response_format, while the Responses API defines the schema under text.format with type, name, schema and strict as sibling properties. question: A legal firm wants a summary of long contracts that contains only sentences that appear verbatim in the original text, ordered by their relevance to the main topic, so lawyers can trace every sentence back to the source. Which Azure Language summarization approach should you use?

options.text: Conversation summarization with the recap aspect
Extractive text summarization, using the rank score to order sentences

explanation: Extractive summarization produces a summary by extracting salient sentences from the source text together with their positional information; each sentence has a rank score that indicates relevance to the main topic, and you can return sentences in their original order or by rank. Abstractive summarization generates new concise sentences that are not verbatim extracts, which breaks traceability. Conversation summarization is for agent/customer transcripts.

question: A call center wants to automatically produce, for each support chat, a short statement of the customer's problem and a separate statement of the troubleshooting steps the agent tried. Which Azure Language conversation summarization aspects should you request?
explanation: Issue/resolution summarization is the call-center-specific feature of conversation summarization: the issue aspect summarizes the customer problem and the resolution aspect summarizes the solutions tried by the agent. recap produces a single paragraph summary of the whole conversation, while chapterTitle and narrative segment the conversation into topical chapters with titles and per-segment summaries. Extractive and abstractive are text summarization approaches, not conversation aspects.

question: An agent in Microsoft Foundry is connected to the Azure Language MCP server. A user sends the prompt "Determine the language of this article and tell me what people are mentioned." Place the steps of the tool selection process in the order they occur.

The agent analyzes the prompt and determines which task or tasks need to be performed
The MCP server processes the request with the appropriate Azure Language capability and returns the results
The agent checks the available MCP tools and their descriptions to find the best match
The agent calls the selected tool(s) through the MCP server, passing the input text

explanation: After the user sends a prompt, the agent analyzes it to determine the required tasks, checks the catalog of MCP tools and descriptions it received at connection time (dynamic tool discovery), calls the selected tool(s) through the MCP server, the server runs the Azure Language capability and returns results, and the agent synthesizes them into a response. The Azure Language MCP server, which exposes language detection, NER, PII redaction and Text Analytics for Health as tools

question: A retailer analyzes product reviews with Azure Language sentiment analysis. The review "The battery life is great but the screen scratches easily" is returned as mixed at document level. The retailer wants to know specifically that battery life was rated positively and the screen negatively. Which feature provides this?

options.text: Extractive summarization with a sentence count of 2
Opinion mining (aspect-based sentiment analysis), which links sentiment to specific targets in the text
Named Entity Recognition with the Product category

explanation: Opinion mining is a feature of sentiment analysis, also called aspect-based sentiment analysis, that provides more granular information about the opinions related to words such as the attributes of products or services. Plain sentiment analysis assigns positive, neutral or negative labels at sentence and document level with confidence scores between 0 and 1, but does not tie sentiment to individual attributes within one sentence. NER identifies entities but not opinions about them.

question: A gaming company wants to scan player chat messages for harmful content and receive a severity level per harm category so that moderators can set different thresholds. Which Azure AI Content Safety API should you call, and which categories does it return?

Analyze text API; returns Person, Organization and Location categories

question: You are designing safety checks for an LLM-based agent with Azure AI Content Safety. For each requirement, select the Content Safety feature that addresses it.

Check whether the model's answer is supported by the source documents the user supplied
Detect AI-generated text that reproduces known song lyrics, recipes or articles
Detect when the agent's tool use is misaligned, unintended or premature in the context of the user interaction

explanation: The Content Safety overview maps features to purposes: Prompt Shields scans text for the risk of a user input attack on an LLM; groundedness detection checks whether LLM responses are grounded in user-provided source material; protected material text detection scans AI-generated text for known content such as song lyrics, articles and recipes; and the Task adherence API detects misaligned, unintended or premature tool use by agents. question: You are implementing multi-language speech-to-speech translation (English speech into both French and Japanese audio) with the Azure Speech SDK for Python using the manual synthesis approach. Put the steps in the order in which each one depends on the previous.

items.text: Call translator.recognize_once_async().get() to capture the utterance and obtain translation_results.translations
Create a SpeechTranslationConfig with the Foundry key and endpoint, set speech_recognition_language to en-US and call add_target_language for fr and ja

Create a separate SpeechConfig and AudioOutputConfig(use_default_speaker=True); then for each language in the translations dictionary set speech_synthesis_voice_name to a language-specific voice and call SpeechSynthesizer(speech_cfg, audio_out_cfg).speak_text_async(text).get()
Create a TranslationRecognizer from the translation config and an AudioConfig that uses the default microphone

explanation: Manual synthesis combines two operations: a TranslationRecognizer (built from a SpeechTranslationConfig with source and target languages plus an AudioConfig) translates spoken input into text in each target language, and then you iterate through the Translations in the result, using a SpeechSynthesizer with a language-specific voice to speak each one. A separate SpeechConfig and AudioConfig are required for the synthesis API. Event-based synthesis would not work here because it only supports 1:1 translation to a single target language.

Set speech_config.speech_synthesis_voice_name on a SpeechConfig and call recognize_once_async() on a SpeechRecognizer
Pass an AudioOutputConfig to the TranslationRecognizer constructor so audio is played automatically
Set translation_cfg.voice_name to a French voice such as fr-FR-HenriNeural and connect a handler to the TranslationRecognizer's synthesizing event, reading evt.result.audio

explanation: Event-based synthesis is used for 1:1 translation: you specify the desired voice via voice_name on the SpeechTranslationConfig, create an event handler for the TranslationRecognizer's synthesizing event, and in the handler retrieve the translated audio bytes from the result (the module's example writes evt.result.audio to a file). Connect the tool in the portal and select Always approve all Azure Language in Foundry Tools tools

question:
You are writing SSML for an Azure Speech synthesis request so that one neural voice speaks cheerfully, the word SQL is pronounced as sequel, and a short pause is inserted. Complete the markup and the SDK call.

<speak version="1.0" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2001/10/synthesis" xmlns:mstts="https://www.w3.org/2001/mstts" xml:lang="en-US">
  <voice name="en-US-AriaNeural">
    <[B1] style="cheerful">Welcome back!</[B1]>
    Open <[B2] alphabet="sapi" ph="s iy k w ax l">SQL</[B2]> Server.
    <[B3] strength="weak"/>Let's begin.
  </voice>
</speak>

result = speech_synthesizer.[B4](ssml).get()

blanks.prompt: Element that sets a speaking style for a neural voice
Element that specifies a phonetic pronunciation

explanation: SSML lets you specify a speaking style with mstts:express-as (for example cheerful) when using a neural voice, give phonetic pronunciations with the phoneme element, insert pauses with the break element, adjust pitch and rate with prosody, and apply say-as rules for dates or numbers. To submit SSML you use speak_ssml_async on the SpeechSynthesizer; speak_text_async is for plain text.

question: A telephony integration requires synthesized speech from Azure Speech as 24 kHz, 16-bit mono PCM in a RIFF (WAV) container, spoken by the en-US-Brian:DragonHDLatestNeural voice. Which Python code configures this on an existing speech_config object?
explanation: The SpeechConfig object customizes synthesized audio: set_speech_synthesis_output_format() takes a SpeechSynthesisOutputFormat enumeration value (such as Riff24Khz16BitMonoPcm, which encodes the file type, sample rate and bit depth), and the speech_synthesis_voice_name property selects the voice by its locale/name identifier. speech_recognition_language configures recognition, not synthesis, and AudioOutputConfig only determines where audio is sent.

question: You want to transcribe a recorded meeting (speech.mp3) using a generative AI speech model deployed in Microsoft Foundry, via the OpenAI Python SDK's AzureOpenAI client. Which model family and method should you use?

options.text: A gpt-4o-transcribe (or gpt-4o-mini-transcribe / gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize) deployment with client.audio.transcriptions.create(model=..., file=audio_file, response_format="text")
A gpt-4o-mini-tts deployment with client.audio.speech.with_streaming_response.create(model=..., voice="alloy", input=...)

explanation: Speech-to-text models in Microsoft Foundry include gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe and gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize; you open the audio file in binary mode and pass it to client.audio.transcriptions.create() with the deployment name and a response_format such as text. gpt-4o-tts and gpt-4o-mini-tts are text-to-speech models used with client.audio.speech, which is the reverse operation.

question: You are connecting the Azure Speech MCP Server to a Foundry agent so it can transcribe audio and generate spoken responses. Which three items are required or recommended by the setup? (Choose three.)

options.text: A SAS URL for the container with Read, Add, Create, Write and List permissions, supplied as the X-Blob-Container-Url value
A Cosmos DB account to store transcripts
A custom speech endpoint deployed in Speech Studio
An Azure Storage account with a blob container, because generated audio files are saved to Blob Storage
The Foundry project key supplied as the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key bearer credential

explanation: Unlike text-only MCP tools, the Azure Speech MCP server works with audio files, so it needs an Azure Storage account and blob container (text-to-speech output is saved there and speech-to-text can read from a SAS URL). When you connect the tool you provide the Foundry resource name, the project key as the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key bearer value, and the container SAS URL (Read, Add, Create, Write, List) as X-Blob-Container-Url. Cosmos DB and a custom speech endpoint are not part of the setup.

question: A developer upgrades a Python app to the latest azure-cognitiveservices-speech package and wants to create the SpeechConfig object using the Foundry resource endpoint instead of a region name. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The endpoint must be passed to AudioConfig, and SpeechConfig takes only the key
Endpoint-based configuration requires Microsoft Entra ID and cannot be used with a key
SpeechConfig(subscription=KEY, endpoint=ENDPOINT) is supported; releases prior to 1.48.2 required the region instead of the endpoint
SpeechConfig only accepts a region; the endpoint must be set later with set_property

explanation: The SpeechConfig object encapsulates the connection details; in the module it is created with speech_sdk.SpeechConfig(subscription="YOUR_FOUNDRY_KEY", endpoint="YOUR_FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT"). The note explains that Python SDK releases prior to 1.48.2 required you to specify the region where the resource is deployed, whereas the latest release accepts either the Foundry resource endpoint or the region. AudioConfig defines the audio source or destination, not the service connection.

question: You are building a browser-based voice assistant that connects directly to the Voice Live API over WebSocket and must use keyless Microsoft Entra authentication. Which configuration is correct?

options.text: Obtain a token for the https://management.azure.com/.default scope and pass it in the model query parameter
Send the resource key in an api-key connection header on the prehandshake connection
Assign the Storage Blob Data Contributor role and pass a SAS URL as the api-key query parameter
Assign the Cognitive Services User role, obtain a token for the https://ai.azure.com/.default scope, and send it as Authorization: Bearer <token> on the WebSocket request

explanation: For keyless authentication with Microsoft Entra ID you assign the Cognitive Services User role to the user or managed identity, generate a token with the https://ai.azure.com/.default scope (or the legacy https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default scope), and send it in the Authorization header as Bearer <token>. The api-key connection header on the prehandshake connection is explicitly not available in a browser environment; in a browser a key would have to go in the api-key query string parameter instead.

question: You are implementing a Python client for a Voice Live agent using the azure-ai-voicelive async client library and PyAudio. Arrange the runtime flow of the client in the correct order, starting from connection setup and following the first user turn.

items.text: On ServerEventType.SESSION_UPDATED, start microphone capture; each captured chunk is base64-encoded and sent with connection.input_audio_buffer.append(audio=...)
Open the connection with connect(endpoint=..., credential=..., agent_config={"agent_name": ..., "project_name": ...})
On ServerEventType.RESPONSE_AUDIO_DELTA, queue event.delta for playback; on RESPONSE_AUDIO_DONE the response is complete
Send a RequestSession via connection.session.update() specifying modalities, PCM16 audio formats, turn detection, echo cancellation and noise reduction
When the user starts speaking (ServerEventType.INPUT_AUDIO_BUFFER_SPEECH_STARTED), clear any pending playback so the agent does not talk over the user

explanation: The recommended pattern connects to the agent (Entra ID credential plus agent_config with agent_name and project_name), configures the session with a RequestSession through session.update(), and then processes server events: SESSION_UPDATED triggers audio capture that appends base64 audio to the input buffer, INPUT_AUDIO_BUFFER_SPEECH_STARTED is handled by clearing pending playback so the client does not keep playing the last response during an interruption, and RESPONSE_AUDIO_DELTA chunks are queued for playback until RESPONSE_AUDIO_DONE.

Noise reduction type that filters background noise from input audio
Metadata key prefix under which the Voice Live configuration is stored (chunked into 512-character entries)

explanation: The Voice Live session uses turn_detection type azure_semantic_vad for intelligent turn detection, input_audio_noise_reduction type azure_deep_noise_suppression to filter background noise (which also improves VAD accuracy), and input_audio_echo_cancellation type server_echo_cancellation.
